citation.text: Li M, Long B, Dai SY, Golden JW, Wang X, Yuan JS. Altered carbon partitioning enhances CO2 to terpene conversion in cyanobacteria. BioDesign Res 2022;2022:9897425.

units: DTASelect spectral counts per million filtered spectra in the run, mean of three biological replicates

temperature.text: not restated for the log/stationary samples; the strains' general cultivation (Methods 2.2) was at 30 °C

lightIntensity.text: not restated for the log/stationary samples; general cultivation was 75 µmol photons m-2 s-1 in flasks, then 100 in a Roux bottle

lightRegime.text: continuity, photoperiod and spectrum not reported

co2.text: not restated for the log/stationary samples; general cultivation bubbled 5% CO2 at 50 mL/min in the Roux bottle

medium.text: not restated for the log/stationary samples; general cultivation used BG11 with 10 mM TES, pH 8.2

format.text: not restated for the log/stationary samples; general cultivation went from 250 mL flasks to a 1-L Roux bottle

caveat: Measured in L1118, an engineered limonene-producing derivative of PCC 7942, not in wild type and not in UTEX 2973; the strain's heterologous limonene synthase is among the identified proteins and does not map. Label-free spectral counts from an LTQ ion trap (ProLuCID search, DTASelect filter, PatternLab), a coarse abundance measure; a protein has a value only where all three replicates identified it. Decoy entries are dropped and contaminant entries do not map. The growth conditions of these samples are not restated for the comparison (Package B row 73).
